newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX crude called up on technical strength, Brent.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX crude called up on technical strength, Brent.

text.p: NYMEX crude was called to open higher Wednesday, bouncing from technical support levels tested Tuesday and drawing strength from gains in IPE Brent futures.
Higher gasoil futures on IPE was expected to push up refined product here, dealers said.
Crude was called up 20 to 25 cents a barrel, with heating oil up 0.50 to 0.75 cent a gallon and gasoline 0.25 to 0.50 cent higher.
"It's a mixture of some good technical support, and gains in London," said a dealer.
At 0921 EST, December Brent was 29 cents higher at $23.12 a barrel, with December gasoil up $2.75 at $213.50 a tonne.
"We could see some real strength at the open, but things will calm down after that, ahead of the APIs," said a dealer.
API delayed its weekly oil inventory data to Wednesday afternoon from Tuesday because not enough companies had reported data due to the U.S. Veteran's Day holiday Monday.
Tuesday, December crude ended off two cents at $23.35 a barrel. December heat ended off 0.10 cent at 68.25 cents and December gasoline ended up 0.75 cent at 65.77 cents a gallon.
Dealers said nearby crude was technically strong with Tuesday's low higher than Monday's. Support for Dec crude was pegged at $23.15 and resistance around $24.00.
Dealers said trading may be as lackluster as Tuesday as traders step to the sidelines awaiting the API stock data.
"We may be fairly rangebound today," said a trader.

The market focus for the API data remains distillate inventory, which heating oil is a part. For the week ended November 8, traders are expecting distillate inventories to be unchanged to one million barrels higher.
-- Harry Milling, New York Energy Desk, 212-859-1761
